solution:
Use integration by parts with $u=x$, $dv=\cos x\,dx$, so $du=dx$ and $v=\sin x$:
$$\int_{0}^{\pi/2}x\cos x\,dx=\bigl[x\sin x\bigr]_{0}^{\pi/2}-\int_{0}^{\pi/2}\sin x\,dx.$$
Now $\bigl[x\sin x\bigr]_{0}^{\pi/2}=\tfrac{\pi}{2}\cdot1-0=\tfrac{\pi}{2}$, and
$$\int_{0}^{\pi/2}\sin x\,dx=\bigl[-\cos x\bigr]_{0}^{\pi/2}=-(0-1)=1.$$
Therefore the integral equals $\tfrac{\pi}{2}-1$.
hints: Let u = x so that du = dx.
Integrate cos x to get sin x.
Evaluate the boundary term and the remaining integral.
